summary: Expiry cuts through every layer of the create and redirect paths. The Link entity and schema need a nullable expires_at column (new Flyway V2; V1 is applied history). LinkService.create must compute expiresAt from the request TTL, and LinkService.resolve must enforce it. The redirect path is cache-first via LinkCache storing ResolvedLink, so ResolvedLink must carry expiresAt and the check must run after the cache lookup, not only on cache misses. GlobalExceptionHandler needs a 410 mapping, and the create/metadata DTOs need the new fields.

impactedFiles.reason: Cached redirect data must include expiresAt
TTL on create; expiry enforcement in resolve

dataFlows: Create: LinkController -> LinkService.create(url, alias, ttl) -> Link(expiresAt = now + ttl) -> link.expires_at
Redirect: RedirectController -> LinkService.resolve -> LinkCache.get (hit) or LinkRepository.findByCode (miss) -> expiry check -> 302 or LinkExpiredException -> 410
architecturalNotes: LinkCache entries live up to 10 minutes; caching the expiry instant (not an 'is expired' flag) keeps hits correct
Keep the existing two-argument LinkService.create for current callers (ConcurrentClickCountingTest) by delegating
Clock is injected everywhere, so expiry is testable with a controllable clock
